Invisibility cloaks based on transformation design method guide incident waves through a cloaking shell without scattering or distortion.
Temporal steering is a quantum correlation describing the influence of earlier measurements on later states of a single system.
Temporal steering inequality can be used to detect interactions affecting a quantum system over time.
The temporal steering parameter ST remains maximal (2 for two measurement bases) if the system is undisturbed.
Phase damping of photon polarization inside the cloak causes ST to decay as ST = 1 + e^(-2γt).
The initial polarization state of photons is taken as a maximally mixed state ρ = 1/2(|H⟩⟨H| + |V⟩⟨V|).
Electron spin inside the cloak is modeled to interact coherently with an ancillary spin via Hamiltonian H = ħJ(σ+1σ−2 + σ+2σ−1).
The temporal steering parameter for electron spin varies as ST = [5 + 2 cos(2Jt) + cos(4Jt)] / 4.
The time t that waves spend inside the cloak shell is calculated assuming equal phase delay as in free space.
Temporal steering requires only two mutually unbiased measurement bases, fewer than quantum state tomography.
The classical bound of temporal steering inequality is ST ≤ 1, quantum mechanics allows ST ≤ 2 for two bases.
The study considers both electromagnetic waves and matter waves to demonstrate the method.
Quantum effects like dephasing and coherent coupling are almost inevitable when waves pass through material cloaks.
Temporal steering can detect cloaks without needing synchronized measurement directions between sender and receiver.
Other methods to detect cloaks include measuring coherence loss, frequency range mismatch, spin direction changes, and entanglement degradation.
The paper uses a Markovian master equation with Lindblad form to model phase damping of photon polarization.
The invisibility cloak is assumed to be nearly perfect, making classical detection difficult.
The temporal steering approach provides a feasible quantum method to crack invisibility cloaks.
The cloak detection method is supported by numerical simulations of temporal steering parameter dynamics.
